title: Birhor people - Wikipedia
text: Birhor (or Birhul) are a tribal / Adivasi forest people, traditionally nomadic, living primarily in the Indian state of Jharkhand. They speak the Birhor language, which belongs to the Munda group of languages of the Austroasiatic language family. [3][4]

text: Birhor is a stable indigenous language of India. It belongs to the Austro-Asiatic language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

text: The word Birhor finds its meaning in Mundari Language where it can be seen as a compound of two meaningful words –'Bir' meaning 'forest' and 'Hor' meaning 'the man'.Birhor belongs to the Austro Asiatic language family.
